Enable Drop Down Status Bar in Accessibility settings first.
The service is restarting. Please try again.
Long-press an empty area on the home screen, choose Widgets, then add a Notifications, Quick settings, or combined 1×1 widget.
The accessibility service only requests the Android global action that opens notifications or quick settings. It does not inspect screen content, read notifications, or collect typed text.

Effective date: August 22, 2026

Drop Down Status Bar does not collect, store, transmit, or share personal data. The app has no Internet permission and does not require an account.

Accessibility service
The accessibility service is used only when you request the global Android action to open the notification panel or quick settings. Window content retrieval is disabled. The app does not read notification content, screen content, passwords, or typed text.

Local settings
Your selected default action and vibration preference are stored only on this device. Android backup may preserve these preferences if device backup is enabled.

Permissions
Vibration is used only for optional feedback after a successful action. No notification access, location, contacts, camera, microphone, or storage permission is requested.

You can stop all accessibility functionality at any time by disabling Drop Down Status Bar in Android Accessibility settings.
Opens notifications or quick settings when you tap the app shortcut. Screen content is never retrieved.
